# OBS013 `bad-do-termination`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="enabled by default" />

A labelled `do` loop ends on a statement other than `continue` or `end do`.

## Why

Ending a loop on an action statement (an assignment, a write) was deleted in Fortran 2018 and
makes the last iteration's work easy to misread as following the loop.

## Reported

```fortran
do 10 i = 1, n
10 a(i) = 0.0
```

## Preferred

```fortran
do i = 1, n
  a(i) = 0.0
end do
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[OBS013] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = OBS013` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/fobos/lint).

## Equivalent

Fortitude rule `OB093` (see [Lint Rules](/lint-rules/#relation-to-fortitude)).
